current_answer: Current evidence supports several distinct routes: fal H3 Max Director is a finite hosted context-carrying WebRTC session; Yoroll says H3 Superfast powers YoLive, a group proposal-and-vote route; Reactor FastH3 is a high-end queue-and-playout route; FastVideo documents local FastH3 clip paths and a four-GPU Dreamverse frame-carried Preview v1 profile; a community project reports one RTX 5090 sustaining a retimed dense FastH3 channel; Comfy offers local H3 paths; and vLLM-Omni documents a separate H3 service. vLLM-Omni’s current H3 recipe says step execution can admit requests between denoise steps, but its stated two-H100 test found four simultaneous H3 jobs slower under four-way co-batching than ordinary request mode. Its documented two-RTX-5090 DLO launch selects the FL2VA task path, which serves T2VA and FL2VA, and recommends a 384 GiB host; its one 50-step T2VA validation returned about 5.17 seconds of output in 8 minutes 38 seconds. Treat task path, client capability, arrival pattern, and a recorded output as separate facts. No cited H3 result establishes a live viewer experience. Comfy Org also reports that its H3 VAE encode/decode round trip fell from 24.3 to 12.7 seconds on an RTX 5090 at 1344×768, 129 frames after the v0.36.0 update; this is a VAE-stage A/B, not a full-render or live-speed result. vLLM-Omni v0.30.0 now documents opt-in Ref2VA long-video latent-tail continuation; its maintainer reports one 30.667-second, 736-frame H3 result on eight B300 GPUs. This is a completed-output route with no published full wall time, cost, first frame, or live playout result.

catalogue_card.question: Did H3 become a continuous stream in vLLM-Omni?
catalogue_card.text: No. v0.30.0 adds longer Ref2VA clips through latent-tail continuation. An eight-B300 project test reports 30.667 seconds of output, but not the full wait or a viewer-visible live result.

summary: vLLM-Omni v0.30.0 documents opt-in Ref2VA long-video continuation. Its maintainer reports one 736-frame, 30.667-second original-H3 output on eight B300 GPUs at 1344×768, 24 fps, 50 steps; full wall time and live delivery are not supplied.

Comfy Org reports that the H3 video VAE encode/decode round trip fell from 24.3 to 12.7 seconds on an RTX 5090 at 1344×768, 129 frames after its v0.36.0 update. This is one stage, not whole-job speed.

vLLM-Omni says H3 can admit and retire requests between denoise steps, but its stated two-H100 test with four simultaneous 672×384, 209-frame, 30-step requests reports worse wall time and mean latency under four-way co-batching than ordinary request mode.
The source says staggered-arrival behavior remains unmeasured. The benchmark does not predict two RTX 5090 GPUs, a different job shape, a FastH3 adapter, a browser-visible result, or a public stream.

The current two-RTX-5090 DLO launch selects the FL2VA DiT; T2VA uses that path. The source recommends a 384 GiB host, while its one 50-step T2VA validation returned 124 1344×768 / 24 fps frames in 8 minutes 38 seconds.
vLLM-Omni’s current ComfyUI client still accepts one FL2VA frame even though the server recipe can represent ordered first-and-last-frame inputs.
uncertainty: The eight-B300 long-video example is project-maintained and was not independently inspected or timed by the pool. The 300-second request limit is not a validated five-minute result.

The ComfyUI VAE speed figures are provider-maintained node-level A/B measurements on one RTX 5090 setup. Full H3 render time, quality under a pinned workflow, repeated-run reliability, and cost impact remain unmeasured.
The batching result is one project-maintained two-H100 benchmark with four simultaneous requests. Staggered arrivals, other job shapes, other hardware, and viewer-visible behavior remain unmeasured.
The documented two-RTX-5090 result is one project-published T2VA validation. The pool did not independently audit its environment, media, timing, or quality.

The two-5090 command selects the FL2VA path; it does not establish a combined multi-task service, Ref2VA, a two-keyframe client workflow, warm performance, streaming, queueing, or first visible frame.
vLLM-Omni’s current ComfyUI client-scope statements come from an open RFC. The pool did not install or test the server or client.
Dreamverse’s FastH3 profile is project documentation; the pool did not install or run it, inspect a generated handoff, or measure buffer, cost, recovery, or uptime.
FastVideo and ComfyUI still conflict on FastH3 8-Step V2 FL2VA scope. The pool did not run a pinned T2VA or FL2VA workflow.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, end-to-end source-to-visible latency measurement, or first-party pool analytics record is available.
